headings.text: Quick summary: who should pick what

text: Quick summary: who should pick what Umbrella — for those who care about automation (Combo Builder, Auto-Cataclysm, Dodger, Kill Stealer), ready-made hero presets, and a quick learning curve. The minimum plan is cheaper — $2.99 for 3 days. Melonity — for experienced users who are used to the classic interface and do not want to re-learn. Longer on the market, but weaker on new modules (no preset-based Combo Builder, weaker MMR Tracker). Below are concrete figures and facts for each parameter. Safety and spoofer The main risk of using any cheat is an HWID ban — a block tied to your hardware identifiers: even after creating a new Steam account you cannot play from the same PC. Here is what both products offer: Umbrella: Spoofer is built into the subscription, masking hard drive serials, MAC address, motherboard ID, and display identifiers. One-click activation through the Loader. Melonity: Spoofer is a separate product — an add-on to the subscription. Functionally similar, but requires manual configuration and sometimes returns "device unverified" after a Windows update. Umbrella cloud configs do not write settings to disk — the anti-cheat scanner finds no traces. Melonity configs are local (.cfg in the game folder), which more frequently triggers heuristic flags. Patch speed after Valve updates Every time Valve releases a Dota 2 update (minor / major / hotfix), every cheat breaks until the cheat developers release their own patch. Downtime is a critical parameter. Umbrella: average delay 6–18 hours. SLA — 72 hours (if exceeded, we extend everyone's subscription). Melonity: average delay 12–36 hours. Sometimes longer (after patch 7.39 — 4 days of downtime). The reason: Umbrella has a more compact reverse-engineering team that ships patches as binary cloud updates. Melonity uses a traditional full-build rebuild. Support Parameter Umbrella Melonity Live chat on site Yes, 10:00–23:00, reply in 5–10 min Telegram bot, 10:00–22:00 Contact channel live chat, reply in minutes Via ticket system Knowledge base Blog + 126 hero pages FAQ only Response SLA Within 1 hour on business days Up to 24 hours Phishing complaints the live chat on the Support page Via general ticket Verdict If you are choosing a cheat for Dota 2 in 2026 for the first time — go with Umbrella . Cheaper, more modules out of the box, faster patches, better support, spoofer at no extra charge. If you have been using Melonity for years and love their interface — migrating to Umbrella takes about an hour. Umbrella cloud configs support importing Melonity presets (via a convert command through support). Known downsides of Umbrella to be aware of: No mobile app for config management (on the roadmap for Q2 2026; Melonity does not have one either). Localization is Russian/English only (Melonity supports CN/KR — but that is not critical for most Western users). ★ Recommendation: start with Umbrella's 3-day plan ($2.99) . That is enough to test the interface, maphack, and scripts on your favorite hero. If you do not like it — try Melonity without a serious loss. FAQ Can you use Umbrella and Melonity at the same time? No. Both inject into the same Dota 2 process and conflict. Choose one. Which is safer from a ban perspective? As of 2026, ban rates are comparable across both products: ~3% ban rate with proper use of a spoofer. The main factor is not the brand, but following the rules (not feeding perfect stats, not getting reported, not using it on a main account). Which has a better Skin Changer? Umbrella's catalog is larger (2400+ vs 1800+ for Melonity). Skin application works stably in both. If you only need a Skin Changer without scripts — check out Overplus (from $0.30).
